title: On Discovering Algorithms for Adversarial Imitation Learning
venue: The Fourteenth International Conference on Learning Representations

publication.venue: The Fourteenth International Conference on Learning Representations

mechanism.domainTask: LLM-guided evolutionary discovery of reward-assignment functions for adversarial imitation learning
mechanism.populationDetail: A common pool of reward-assignment functions is updated generation by generation; no island or tree structure is described.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No separate archive is described; the top-K survivors constitute the next population.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Each generation selects top K from the union of the old population and newly generated crossover candidates.
mechanism.generationDetail: The LLM is prompted with two parent reward-function programs and their scores to synthesize one new function semantically.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Parent fitness is included as scalar performance scores in the crossover prompt; lower Wasserstein divergence is better, represented as a higher-is-better score in the example.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Algorithm 2 says to randomly sample parent pairs from the current population; it does not state whether sampling is with replacement. Do not confuse this with the separate top-K survivor-selection step.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/ON DISCOVERING ALGORITHMS FOR ADVERSARIAL IMITATION LEARNING.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Existing survey citations place DAIL under multi-parent fusion and parent selection. Also consider flat-population and generational-replacement coverage. Parent pairs are randomly sampled; top-K fitness ranking selects survivors, not parents. The score in the prompt is a sign-converted scalar fitness derived from lower-is-better Wasserstein distance.
